goal: One short sentence on how it helps, then one open question about what they are building. No product names, no list, no visual.
Say in the first sentence that it is memory and context for AI agents, then two or three plain points. No interview.

turns: How is this different from RAG?
goal: Lead with the core difference: RAG retrieves static chunks, memory extracts, updates, and forgets facts about a user over time. Mention that both come from one engine. No interview.

turns: Why does it use fewer tokens than keeping memory in markdown files?
goal: Answer that it retrieves only what the question needs instead of re-reading files, so cost per question stays low as memory grows. The token-cost chart directly shows this and should be attached.

turns: Show me how the memory graph works
goal: Explain in two lines that it stores facts and the links between them, with time, then show a memory graph visual.
Give the plan prices first: Free $0, Pro $19, Max $100, Scale $399 a month, Enterprise custom. A plans visual helps. No sales pressure.

turns: Can I run it on my own servers? Our data can't leave our VPC.
goal: Say yes first: a self-hosted local binary with the same API, and air-gap on Enterprise. Keep it short.
Answer yes in the first sentence: SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR. One or two lines. A big unrelated visual would be wrong.

turns: I want my agent to remember stuff
goal: Reflect what they said and ask one question to learn more (what the agent does, or who it remembers). Do not write a plan or list products yet.

turns: I'm building a support chatbot that should remember each customer across conversations

goal: Now give the plan: hosted Memory API first with one reason in their words, then 3-5 numbered steps that include one containerTag per tenant or customer, a stable customId per conversation, and reading the profile each turn. One docs link.

turns: We already use Pinecone and LangChain. Should we just keep chunking there?
goal: Do not tell them to keep chunking. Lead with hosted supermemory memory and profiles for their agent, and mention their stack only as optional. One question at most.

goal: Do not ask again who it remembers or what the app does: they already said tutoring, one memory per student. Move them forward with a first step or the one missing piece.

goal: If the docs do not give a number, say so plainly and point to the docs or the team. Never invent a latency number.

goal: Decline briefly and bring them back to what you can help with: memory for their agent. One short reply, no poem.
